newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends locked up 20 cent limit.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends locked up 20 cent limit.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended locked up their 20-cent per bushel limit as the market surged amid fears that bitter cold temperatures this weekend caused widespread damage to the winter wheat crop.

"This is one of those deals where there's one story and that's it -- the winter wheat crop got some damage and analysts are saying that we might have 100 to 250 million bushels lost as a result," a MGE trader said at the midsession.
Volumes were extremely thin as trading was hampered by the activation of daily limits.

"We traded 47 million bushels in here Friday and maybe eight million today. There was some trade at the open -- maybe 100 million bushels here and there -- but then it just died," another MGE trader said.
Traders said MGE July options traded synthetically 10 to 12 cents per bushel over the MGE July future, which was capped at $4.42.
Traders said the pool of unfilled orders was around five million bushels, with 2.5 million bushels in the July contract. Orders for 1.5 million bushels were pooled in the May contract.
MGE spring wheat settled locked limit up, with May up 20 cents at $4.50. July was up 20 cents at $4.42.
